findings.reasoning: handleKeyDown is a capture listener on the document (29932 `document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown, true);`). The 6207 rename-box listener calls e.stopPropagation() (6208), but capture runs before the target, so handleKeyDown has already processed the key. With focus in the canvas rename input, _alignmentKeysAway() at 16801 is '' (the box is not #busyOverlay and not inside a _KEY_WINDOW_IDS element), so the 16802 guard does not apply. However 16845-16847 finds the focused INPUT, and 16859 with 16864 returns for every key except searchInput Ctrl+F, so viewer shortcuts (undo, delete, selection) cannot fire on the rename box when no job runs and no window is open: Enter commits the rename via finish(true) -> 6205 _commitSeqRename (state.seqs header + pushUndo), Escape (6210) cancels. That is the intended, correct behaviour.
findings.scenario: Double-click a sequence name, type, Enter/Escape: only the rename is committed or cancelled; handleKeyDown stays out of the way (16859-16864). Not reachable while a job runs: onOutside (capture mousedown, removed at 6200) fires on the click that starts the job and the box is gone before #busyOverlay shows.
findings.title: Rename-box keydown (6207): Enter/Escape; capture guard plus 16859 text-entry return cover the normal case

findings.reasoning: The 16807 guard returns at 16818 for every key while keysAway !== '', but 16812-16813 preventDefault only Ctrl/Meta/Alt keys, so a plain Enter is neither consumed nor blocked on its way to target listeners. Any focused input outside a window therefore still fires its own keydown during a job. For the 6207 rename box that would be finish(true) -> _commitSeqRename -> pushUndo while MAFFT runs. I could not construct a concrete trigger: the box registers onOutside as a capture mousedown handler on the document (removed at 6200), and opening the input at 6194 stole focus, so a click starts any job only after the box has already finish()ed. Keyboard-started jobs are also blocked: with focus in the input _isTextEntry triggers 16859/16864 before any align shortcut. So the hole exists structurally (plain keys are passed through during busy) but I found no reachable path.
findings.scenario: No user steps found that leave this box open while #busyOverlay shows; recording the gap as low confidence rather than a confirmed defect.
findings.title: Plain (unmodified) Enter is not preventDefaulted by the busy guard, so an inline input's Enter handler can still run while a job runs

Because handleKeyDown is first in capture (29932), window/user shortcuts are already held off inside this window, so the local stopPropagation is redundant but not harmful. findings.reasoning: The reads jump box is the input with placeholder at 10542 (`'e.g. 1234-1260, chrE:1500-18'`) and its keydown handler pushes Enter into readsJump (callback at 10734, grep-hit `10734: function readsJump(text)`). readsJump only re-registers a reads server-side view/filter: the window's inputs send server-side reads requests and render rows; the script.js/alignment view and uiState it touches are the reads view only. I traced no path into pushUndo, threeKindsOfChange or any state.seqs mutation. Because handleKeyDown registers first in capture (29932 `    document.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown, true);`) and returns at 16859-16864 for this focused text input (or at 16807/16818 busy/window), the viewer's alignment shortcuts never double-fire from keystrokes in the jump box; the local stopPropagation is unnecessary but harmless. Even if #busyOverlay is up, a plain Enter is not preventDefaulted by the busy guard (16812-16813 preventDefault only modifiers), so the reads jump can re-issue while a job runs - but that changes reads rendering only, never seqs, selection or undo (confirmed via the grep for xml_document: [object DOMElement] — related reads DOM callouts only).

note: Audited the keydown listeners at script.js 192, 6207, 9547, 10540, 11176, 11212, 11227, 11283, 14368, 15164 against the Batch-1 guard (handleKeyDown, registered in CAPTURE at 29932, so it runs before every target-phase listener; _alignmentKeysAway guard at 16802/16807/16818; text-entry return at 16859/16864; plain non-modifier keys are never preventDefaulted by the busy guard at 16812-16813). Conclusion: all non-handleKeyDown listeners found are inert with respect to state.seqs, the selection and the undo history — the rename boxes (6207, 14368) are the only ones that write state.seqs (headers) + pushUndo, and they are correctly shielded in the normal case by the 16859 text-entry return and by their capture mousedown outside-handlers (removed at 6200), which prevent them surviving into a running job. The theme edits (resize selection, select, etc.) are recorded as 'low' severity note: the busy guard passes plain keys through to target listeners, which is structurally unsafe for inline inputs, though I could not construct a concrete trigger. Read-filter listeners (11176 context-menu Escape, 11212/11227/11283 filter inputs) and the reads jump box (10540), the chip-box keydown (15164) and the popover close at 192 only touch reads/view/UI chrome; none call push/_pop threeKindsOfChange helpers.
